lens: ATTENTION: does it stop a thumb and hold the eye on a phone, at phone size, in a 30-45 s voice-led film (the first 3 s weigh most; a subtle effect counts as none)

scores.reason: No gaze evidence for thirds (no preference in large photo sets [S3]; raised only experts' interest [AT31]); the first look lands on the centre whatever sits on a third [S7, V5]; on the feed the visible thirds x 393 / 687 are just the axis edges, so the grid adds nothing for the eye; its use is proportion (sky : ground 2:1), not attention.

Works only because the phi box (x 413-667, y 951-1187; on the feed x 436-644, y 951-1168) lies within ~130 px of the centre where the first saccade goes [S7, AT15]; phi itself has no gaze evidence [S4]: the right home for every onset, not a pull of its own.

The nested cut has no attention evidence; the big form is the larger, earlier call and the small subject at its foot (570, 1086) is seen only if it carries the light and the onset (then E2 / RM6 do the work): a two-call risk at phone size.

The eye does not travel a curve, it jumps between key elements [AT31]; in reel 04a the walker at the spiral's eye was only the 4th value call (reels.md section 6); it pulls only when RM1's traveller or RM8's pen rides the arc into the pole, which is their score, not the spiral's.

No gaze evidence; its two feet (454, 987) and (626, 1133) are two related points ~226 px apart, inside the crowding ring (~150-220 px at the 4-6 degree drop [AT25]), and the slope itself outpulls either foot.

An orientation singleton (one strong vertical among level lines builds salience [AT8]) whose crossing is a junction gaze favours [AT13], at x 413-667 near the centre, with the tall frame's full height; but a mast or lamp post is not the subject unless the light or a figure sits at the crossing.

Fixations gather on a single symmetry axis [AT32] and ours is the screen centre x 540 [S7]; a mirrored frame reads as one fluent gist in 0.25 s [AT1, AT59]; its one break at the axis on the turn is a singleton change at the centre; once or twice a film, or it stops reading as an event.

The lines' end gains attention only with a clear subject there (one study, 34 viewers [AT30]); the eye does not ride lines [AT31]; in the owner's reels a brighter patch beat the lines' subject in 12 of 20 frames: it pulls when the lines end within 40 px of the focal's box AND at the story light; drawn live by RM8 it becomes a path the eye can follow.

The vanishing point draws fixations beyond salience (AUC 0.85 vs 0.80) and search is faster there [AT29]; on the subject at x 540-700, y 950-1150 it coincides with the centre bias [S7]; the owner's model explainer centres its VP in 11 of 16 shots (vertical.md section 6); a 5 once the closing object holds the light (E7 + E2).

A convergence point like B2 [AT29] with 5-9 rays, but rays are extra edges (feature clutter cuts attention to the key element [AT26]) and ours must avoid the band (wires only above y 290 or below y 600); it pulls when a light event (RM6) fires at the source.

Stacks a vanishing point [AT29], the brightest area [AT6] and the centre [S7] on the far opening at (540, 950-1100), 15-25 % of the frame; but the portal's sides in the gutters (x < 95, > 945) through the band are mostly cropped on the feed (visible x 98-982), so the enclosure reads only in the stage; the natural set-up for J2.

A texture with no point, no gaze evidence as a guide (attention.md: 1); its one use for the eye is the uniform field that a single mover or a break pops out of (similar distractors make the odd one easy [AT22]): 3-5 lines below y 600 at 30-60 degrees under RM3 or RM1.

Orientation contrast makes the diagonal itself salient [AT8], so the line, not the subject, takes the look unless the focal breaks it at its upper end with the light; no gaze study; its energy is a feeling for the turn, not a pull.

A crossing seen 35-55 degrees down puts a convergence at (540, 1000-1100), but the raised view shrinks everything into many small parts (arms, lamps) and the crossing is a place, not a subject; weak, once a film.
A slow route in; the eye does not ride curves [AT31], so the S works only if its end (480-640, 950-1150) is lit or a traveller (RM1) rides it; calm by design, no thumb-stop.
An enclosure: a surrounded region reads as the figure and is processed fluently [AT59], but the curve is a big shape of its own beside the subject; no gaze study; a calm holding frame.
A frame on two sides: one side mass <= 216 px, partly in the strip the feed crops (x < 98), quieter than the focal; no attention effect of its own beyond keeping the eye inside the stage.

A convergence at the V's point on the focal (within 60 px of (540, 950-1100)), like B2 [AT29], with the band in the open top; the canyon (sky <= 10 %) quiets the sides; inverted it adds unease for the turn.

Its centre (540, 1000-1100) is where the centre bias already puts the eye [S7] and reel 05 opened on it (frame 0), a bold geometric gist; but that reel frame was the busiest measured (11 value calls, 17 % quiet: reels.md section 6) and clutter cuts attention to the key element [AT26]: tone-on-tone ramps and a lit centre, once a film (attention.md: 2).

Its round-window form (300-500 px, centre in the golden box) is a frame within a frame and pulls like C1 when lit; its ring-of-things form puts many small calls round the subject (clutter [AT24]); a circle is also the best match-cut anchor (J3, J4) (attention.md: 2).

One opening on the axis, 15-30 % of the frame, with a figure 150-300 px dark in its aperture, stacks the centre [S7], a person [AT18] and a silhouette step; as catalogued (aperture only >= 10 L* off its rim) it is a 4; lit to E2's >= 65 L* step it is our strongest frame (attention.md: 5 lit, 3 unlit).

A near layer is big and contrasty by nature and pulls off the subject [AT26]; our hint (<= 2 props within 8 L* of the near shade) is quiet, and its home y 1250-1920 lies mostly under the name block (y >= 1519) and the bottom scrim (-10-20 %): no attention value on the feed, only depth.

Two levels are two places: the first saccade splits unless one is tone-on-tone [AT22]; the tall frame fits it (y 700-950 over y 1150-1450) and an onset passing from cause to effect can lead the eye, but the device itself directs nothing.

The subject is the singleton of a uniform field, the least clutter [AT22, AT24], with the words in its sky: one place to look; but it is small (130-220 px, under AR3's 250 px) in a calm frame, and a calm, pretty opening lost ~80 % by 3 s (playbook): it holds a breather, not a thumb (attention.md: 4).

A person, a magnet even when small [AT18, AT19], against a thing >= 0.7 H (>= 1344 px) cut by the top edge, the tall frame's own resource; awe is the high-arousal feeling that holds and is shared [AT48]; the 130-220 px figure needs a calm field round it.

Two equal masses are two equal calls and the first saccade splits [AT22, AT23]; as the frame of a centred subject its <= 216 px wings sit mostly in the strips the feed crops (x < 98, > 982): nothing for the eye.

A balance device, not a pull: the subject stays on the axis (0-130 px off x 540) and the soft counterweight goes high (the hero cloud in a top gutter, its pull < 50 %); it avoids a second call rather than adding attention; never lower right (x > 830 below y 790), where the rail and name block already weigh (attention.md: 3).
A convergence at the apex under the band (y >= 620), but three spots at unequal distances are three calls unless two stay tone-on-tone; no gaze study; stable and calm.

Two fields >= 13 L* apart and their seam: the seam is a strong edge at the subject (good for early contrast [AT6]), but two fields read as two places and, stacked in a tall frame, near a split screen (segmented attention [V6]); it helps meaning more than the eye.

The textbook pop-out: similar distractors make the one break effortless to find [AT22]; the reel's window row had the fewest calls of all (1 value call, 73 % quiet: reels.md section 6); the break lighting on its word in 0.1-0.3 s adds a luminance onset [AT6, AT10] at (413-667, 860-1100): 'this one' in a glance.

Stacks a person [AT18, AT19], a convergence [AT29] and usually the centre on one point (attention.md: 5); but at 130-220 px (~1.8-3 degrees on the feed, under AR3's 250 px) it needs a calm field and a longer hold (>= 4 s, est.): a strong hold, not the hook's subject.

The salience peak and the meaning on one point: the aperture the lightest area below the sky (L* >= 95) with the figure <= 28 inside (a >= 65 L* step) takes the first saccade [AT5, AT6], with the enclosure, a person and the centre; a value step survives the phone's 4:2:0 colour where hue edges blur [V15].

Steady motion does not capture [AT10], so an even, low-contrast flow keeps a hold alive without stealing the still subject; but one mover passing behind takes the eye [AT13], ours is drawn sharp (no blur to melt the flow into texture), and a still thing among movers pops out less than a mover among still things (motion onset is the feature [AT10]) (attention.md: 4).

Facing steers where viewers look [AT20, S9]: 1.5-2x room in front (a right-facing figure at x <= 410 below y 860, because the rail makes x 870 the right edge); our figures face away, so the cue is the head and shoulders only, weaker than a face.

A quieting rule: a near layer within 8 L* of its mass loses salience [AT33]; but on the feed its home (top at y 1450-1650) is mostly under the name block (y >= 1519) and the bottom scrim, which quiet it anyway: little left to gain (attention.md: 3).

Lowering the far planes' contrast (the farthest within ~10-15 L* of the sky) stops them competing with the focal's step [AT8], and near / far is part of the gist read in 19-67 ms [AT1]; a quieting tool with no pull of its own.

The sight line's end is a convergence the eye favours [AT29]; closed by the subject at x 540-700, y 950-1150 it is also near the centre [S7] and never leaks the eye into open sky; a 5 when the closing object holds the story light (E2).

A colour singleton captures even when irrelevant [AT23] and saturation drives arousal [AT49]: one hot accent (C* >= 50 against <= 25, ~3-5 % of the frame, est.) at the focal pops from a tone-on-tone world; as an area it survives 4:2:0 (a thin coloured line would not [V15]); it carries the eye across joins (J4).

One point of motion and every viewer looks at it [S9, AT13]: a locked frame whose only motion is the subject travelling the device's line into the golden box (x 413-667, y 951-1187), its onset on its word [AT10]; the reels' commonest shot (17 of 23 locked or nearly).

A body is a magnet that can outpull the subject [AT18], and ours stands off the axis (x 130-380 or 700-830, by the crop or the rail); its turned head routes the eye on [AT20], but the first saccade may land on it: one fixation of the ~3-5 a 1.7 s look gives the picture (attention.md: 3, risky).

Hands break through inattention [AT18] and the effect landing in the hand at (300-600, 1000-1250) is the beat's onset near the centre: first-person stakes, a native short-form form (P); caution: v3's opening put the effect in the hand and lost ~60 points by 2 s, which the owner read as a bait commercial.

Frame 0's thumb-stop: the subject's line drawing on is a motion onset at the centre [AT10] that the eye can ride (one pen <= ~37 px/f [AT61]) while the gist forms, then the flood is a luminance onset; all five owner reels use it; it works only bold: >= 1 s, peaking after the page settles at ~0.4 s (the 0.3 s pale draw-on was invisible: playbook).

Selective focus does steer the eye to the sharp part [AT33] and blur melts a passing flow into texture, but on the feed value softness (E5) and light (I11) give the same separation; motion blur would smear our movers' onset edges, and a soft near layer at y >= 1450 sits under the name block anyway.

Words are the second magnet (11.1x fixations [AT16]) and we already spend them on the captions (~30 % of viewing time [AT21]); a title over the shot is text against text, pulls the eye off the subject and repeats the spoken line (the owner: 'why do we have the text repeat itself?'): it costs the hook.

The first look after every picture or cut lands at the centre whatever it holds [S7, AT15], and in vertical video a centred subject got longer fixations and fewer saccades than a moving one [V5]; the focal within 130 px of (540, 960) is also the only area clear in every app view (x 130-870 to y 1519): zero search.

Words above (the band y 290-600), story below (y 600-1520): the eye always knows where both are, as in the owner's model explainer (37-43 % flat sky over a centred stage: vertical.md section 6), so a new frame costs no search; structure, not a pull.

Keeping the horizon off y 900-1020 keeps a long level edge from crossing the focal's home and competing with its step, and setup A sets heads against the sky, a clean silhouette for people [AT18]; otherwise no attention effect.

The eye travels band-to-subject at every caption page (one every ~1.1-1.5 s, ~20-40 times a film): a 300-450 px drop (4-6 degrees) keeps the subject in the preview field while reading, and words near their picture help (d ~0.79-1.10 [AT34]; [V9]); 650 px is the far limit; nothing may call in the drop.

Depth up the tall frame keeps the 884 visible px of width for the one subject and stops two people standing at one depth (two equal calls); near / far is gist [AT1]; the pull belongs to E6, I12 and I4, not to the stacking.

The gist comes from the big masses in 19-67 ms [AT1, AT3] and early saccades go to the strongest contrast [AT6]: one closed shape nameable at 0.25 scale (270 px), the focal's step >= 65 L*, three masses >= 85 % at a squint; value edges survive the phone's 4:2:0 encode where hue edges blur [V15]: it passes the 0.25 s flash test (AR1).

Big, centred and alone: one object >= 650 px (>= 60 % W; AR3 asks >= 400 px of the hook) on one quiet backing with a calm ring and nothing named within ~150-220 px (the crowding distance [AT25]); the platforms' own advice ('tight framing', 'focus on your main subject' [V1]); size alone is a mixed lever for pictures [AT27], so the onset still lands on it.

The colossus >= 0.7 H cut by the top fills the tall frame and reads as power, an awe that holds [AT48]; but the subject is a big mass, not a point, so the eye needs the light or the one tiny mover (0.01-0.02 H) to land.
An overview (35-55 degrees down from a 3rd-5th floor) shrinks everything into many small parts; it helps the eye only as the uniform field of a pattern or a crossing (D7, B7); once a film.

An opening of 15-30 %, >= 10 L* off its surround, pulls like a frame within a frame, and the figure facing it routes its own pull there [AT20]; but the person in the refuge and the opening are two calls, and the frame is calm by design.

The eye re-finds a known frame at once (no search after the cut [AT15]; few sets re-framed: vertical.md section 6) and the one change sits at the focal, where it must be the hardest step or the cut hides it; the callback rewards the viewer's memory: before and after in one look.

The focal at x 250-380 or 700-830 is 160-290 px off the centre, so the first saccade misses it unless an onset marks it [AT15]; at 700-830 it sits by the rail (x 870 below y 860); the unease is felt but costs the look.

The short-sided figure at x 130-300 faces out of the frame and gaze cues send attention where it looks [AT20]: out, toward the crop at x 98; the low-quadrant form is a singleton under a quiet field (D1-like); unease once, on the turn.

Awe holds and spreads [AT48] and the simplest masses (three masses, one call) read in a glance [AT1]; but the 'you' at 60-150 px is 0.8-2 degrees on the feed and the frame is calm: a 1.5-4 s scale beat mid-film, not a thumb-stop.
The working wide (the subject 290-670 px tall in its place) has no attention lever of its own; its value for the eye is the familiar home place, re-found without search.

The explainer's working size: a subject box 270-460 px wide (35-60 % of the stage) is big enough to read what it does at phone size ('tight framing' [V1]), on one backing with <= 2 props: size and quiet, both moderate levers.

A number or chart filling the stage: text pulls 11.1x and gains with its size [AT16, AT27], and words with the picture at the same moment help most (d ~1.22-1.30 [AT34]); a 120-160 px number on what it measures is the proof the eye lands on; one per shot or it competes with the captions.

A ~650 px sun disc at (580, 1060), the brightest area [AT6], centred and huge, behind three values only: the clearest gist we can draw [AT1]; but it is calm (locked 2.5-3 s, clouds ~6 px/s) and the sun is the subject only on a time or ending line; once a film.

One lit person in a dark vastness stacks a spotlight cue [AT36], a person [AT18] and a singleton on the axis, but the shaft as catalogued is +2-4 L*, near invisible at phone size and banded by the encode (a subtle effect counts as none): only a bright pool on the figure carries it.

Two stages split attention into a 'segmented' switching mode [V6] and a subject moving round a vertical frame costs saccades [V5]; on 884 visible px each stage is half-size: it hurts both the stop and the hold.

A rolled horizon is a whole-frame change with no place to look, and on a tall phone frame it reads as a mistake rather than a cue; the turn's unease comes from B6 or N15 with the subject still near the axis.

A parallel projection has no vanishing point and no size falloff, so nothing converges on the subject [AT29] and every part is an equal call [AT22, AT26]; detached and person-less (no people magnet, no awe).

Steep converging verticals are a dramatic pointer, but their third vanishing point sits up in the band or above the frame, so they lead the eye up through the words and out of the top; N11's parallel verticals keep the awe with the eye in the stage.

One point of motion takes every viewer's eye [S9, AT13], its start captures [AT10] and self-propelled, animate motion captures more [AT14]: a walker at ~150 px/s (2.5 px/f) crossing an opening in 1-2 s, its onset on its word, ending in the golden box, with the camera locked so it is the only motion.

An even flow (far walkers 12-50 px/s, clouds 0-15 px/s) does not capture [AT10] and keeps a hold from going dead; but each edge entry (~0.6 a second) is a small onset, one mover right behind the subject steals it [AT13], and drawn sharp our flow pulls more than the reels' blurred one did.

The subject held within +-40 px while the world slides keeps the eye still (centred beats moving in vertical video [V5]); but the whole background moves (no onset, more load), sideways is costly in an 884 px wide view (detail <= ~6.4 px/f), and never two in a row.

Looming captures [AT11]: the field expands round a target held within +-40 px, which becomes the still singleton, on its word with the picture ~0.1 s ahead; it must be big enough to see: >= 3 % in <= 2 s is the floor (1.4 %/s read frozen), the payoff push larger, up to 2x.
8-15 px/s, under the capture threshold on purpose: steady motion does not capture [AT10]; it keeps a hold from reading as a still image without spending the eye, but as an effect it counts as none.

A luminance onset at the focal: a lamp or window on in 0.1-0.3 s (6-18 f) with its bloom, making the frame's hardest step (>= 65 L*); early saccades go to contrast [AT6], onsets capture [AT10], a light that comes with the action is the cue that helps [AT36, AT37], and its sound on the same frame makes it pop out [AT39]; >= 0.5 s from any other onset [AT40].

It hands the motion to the subject, so its onset is the one singleton (one motion leads at a time: attention.md section 8), and a stable centred frame gets longer fixations [V5]; on its own a hold is calm and must carry slow life and a story change every ~1.5-3 s.

The opening's engine: ONE pen tip at ~12-25 px/f the eye can pursue (smooth pursuit to ~37 px/f [AT61]), a draw-on >= 1 s peaking after 0.4 s, then pops (~7 % overshoot) and builds, each a motion or looming onset at the subject [AT10, AT11]; animating the process itself helps learning (d ~0.40 [AT38]); separate reads >= 0.5 s apart [AT40].

A wandering, zooming frame (16-83 px/s, +-0.3-6 %/s) is continuous global motion: it captures nothing [AT10], adds saccades and load (as a moving subject does in vertical video [V5]) and hides the subject's own onsets in the wobble.

Receding motion does not capture by itself [AT11], but the reveal is the film's awe moment (awe holds and spreads [AT48]) with the subject held as the pivot (I12) and its own event (a light burst before the landing, the landmark rising on the payoff word); bold (the far plane slides 1.0 W); once a film.

A vertical reveal suits the tall frame and holds by curiosity [AT60] (600-900 px in 3.5-4.5 s, front-loaded), but the whole frame moves with no local onset, the band must stay one flat field while it travels, and 3.5-4.5 s is long against a 1.7 s look.

The expected wall, then the world opening past it: a reveal that pays curiosity [AT60] with strong parallax (a 400-700 px crane, the ledge 1.3x); the near mass sliding out does not capture [AT11], so the landing needs its own event and the subject where the eye already is.

It moves the eye without a cut: the new focal reaches the hardest step (>= 65 L*) while the old drops >= 10-15 L*, a luminance onset where the eye should go [AT6, AT10] and the cue that improved comprehension even of what it did not light [AT36]; no join, so no reset and no search [AT15]; one at a time, >= 0.5 s apart.

During any move the subject stays within +-40 px of its screen spot, so the eye never re-searches (centred beats moving in vertical video [V5]) and the subject is the still point among moving planes [S6]; it makes every camera move safe for the eye rather than pulling by itself.

Its one gain for the eye, the subject held still while the background moves, is I12's, which a plain push or pull gives; the stretch itself is global motion with no onset at the subject [AT10], and in our 2.5D planes it shows only as planes scaling, weak at 884 visible px unless large.

A slow automatic zoom (1.00 -> 1.06 over 2 s) is ongoing motion that captures nothing [AT10]; on every shot it habituates and empties the story push (RM4) of its contrast: attention spent with no event.

The capture is real (looming [AT11]; camera changes raise arousal [AT46]), but on every key word it lands on the caption page's own onset, wears out within a few uses, and a fast pace with arousing content overloads viewers [AT46]; its one earned form is RM4 on the payoff word.

A black card for 0.6-1.3 s is a still frame with no subject (deadframes flags > 0.4 s); in a feed a black frame reads as the end and invites the swipe, and the next idea must be found from scratch [AT15]; its line-first rhythm survives in T and RM8.
Two half-contrast pictures and no onset: two weak calls at once with no single place to look [AT22]; nothing captures the eye and the subject's step halves while it runs.

A cut is an involuntary orienting response [AT46]; the eye resets to the centre and searches [AT15]; with the new focal near (540, 960), the incoming camera already moving and a 6-20x scale jolt it is the 'But' felt as surprise [AT47]; at most 2 a film or it becomes a search tax.

The seam hides the end, so the minority who reach it (19-25 % in v1) restart before they swipe (P), and the 0.5 s un-build then the >= 1 s draw-on are bold onsets; but it does nothing for the first 3 s, where most viewers leave.

No cut means no reset and no search (the join is the eye's most expensive moment [AT15]); the subject stays the pivot within +-40 px and camSpeed >= ~1 px/f carries across the seams; the swipe window wants one continuous shot until the idea lands; the refresh must then come from the subject's events (every ~1.5-3 s).

A looming push (to 7x in 0.5 s) into the brightest area below the sky captures [AT6, AT11], and the next focal comes out where the aperture was (within 150 px), so the eye never re-searches [AT41]; bold at phone size (1.1 s, the opening 15-30 % of the frame), and 'going inside' pays curiosity [AT60].

The anchor holds its spot (within 150 px and 1.5x) across a 0-frame cut, so the eye is already on the next subject (no search [AT15, AT41]) and the match is a small surprise; a shape alone is weaker early salience than a light, so it is best when the anchor is also the brightest thing (J4).

Each quick cut is an orienting event [AT46] while the pinned anchor (+-10 px) keeps the eye still; but cuts 20-30 f apart fall inside the attentional blink (~0.5 s [AT40]), so the changes round the anchor must be big to register; untested in our >= 3.5 s panels.

The brightest shape or the one hot accent holds its spot across the cut (centre within 190 px, size within 1.5x), so the frame's salience peak at ~0.3 s [AT5, AT6] is exactly where the eye already is: zero search, and the light or accent is the thread itself (E8); the strongest cut-type carrier for the eye.

A continuity cut on a motion onset goes unseen a third of the time [AT42]: the motion (begun >= 4-6 f before, running >= 0.3 s after, in the same screen direction) carries the eye through the cut; rare for us, since our size changes come by pushes.

A held look (>= 0.5 s) cues where the next view is [AT20, S9] and builds curiosity for it; ours are figures from behind, so the cue is the head turn only, weaker than a face, and the next focal must land within 150 px of the gaze's end.

The one mover leads the eye through the cut [AT42], but it takes the eye to the frame's edges, where the feed crops (x 98 / 982) and the rail sits (x >= 870 below y 860), and the re-entry forces a jump across the whole width (~12 degrees, against AR13's ~220 px); vertical carries cross the band and the name block.

A big moving edge (>= 70 % of the stage at ~50 px/f) is a bold onset that leaves the eye where it stops (attention.md section 8, est.), so the next focal must be there; it carries no information itself, and the near mass is the call for its ~0.5 s.
A full-frame onset with no place to look (attention.md section 8: never): energy, then the eye must re-find the subject; drawn without blur it is a 2-3 f smear, nearer a flash than a carry.

One object the eye tracks through the whole join (position, then shape and colour, then the world, in 0.4-0.8 s), the brightest and hottest thing throughout: no reset, no search; the transformation itself is the onset [AT10] and 'this IS that' is the surprise [AT47]; animating a real change helps learning [AT38].

A luminance onset in a frame the eye already knows (no reset): a lamp in 0.1-0.3 s or the sky by a moving edge over ~0.8-1.5 s, the cue moving with the event [AT36, AT37]; a whole-sky change must end with the hardest step on the subject, or it is a full-frame change with no place to look.
The paper keeps its spot, so the eye stays (no search), and the turn is a motion event at the focal, a familiar 'next page' gesture; limited to paper beats.

A sound on a change makes that change pop out even in clutter [AT39] (the effect on its frame or 1-2 f after), and the next place's ambience arriving 0.2-0.5 s early primes the cut; ducked under the voice the bridge itself is quiet: it supports the eye's carriers rather than leading.

A spin, glitch, RGB split or flash is a full-frame onset with no place to look (attention.md sections 4 and 8: never in the swipe window); it spends the orienting response on nothing, and flashes > 3 a second risk viewers' safety.

notes: SCALE (attention only). 5 = stacks >= 2 proven levers (a motion or light onset, the centre, the brightest area / hardest value step, a person, a singleton, words with their picture) on the subject and works at phone size in the first 3 s or at a key beat; 4 = one strong proven lever on the subject, or a stack held back by size or frequency; 3 = helps indirectly (where it puts the subject, what it quiets) or one study, or strong with a real split / clutter risk; 2 = little attention power of its own, or a real pull spent at a cost; 1 = hurts in our frame (splits the eye, competes with the captions, a full-frame onset with no place to look, a dead or wobbling frame) or does nothing for the eye. DISTRIBUTION: 14 x 5 (13.6 %: 7 the owner's, 7 ours), 20 x 4, 30 x 3, 24 x 2, 15 x 1; means: the owner's 58 at 2.84, ours 45 at 3.07 (ours include 9 of the 14 rejected tools; the owner's include the five pure placement grids). GROUNDS: attention.md (levers L1-L15, rules AR1-AR18, section 7's 41 scores, section 8's moves) and vertical.md (the feed shows x 98-982 only; the rails cover x >= 870 below y 860 and x >= 945 from y 790; the name block from y 1519 with a 10-20 % scrim under it; the swipe settles at ~0.4 s; 1 degree = 74 px; the drop 300-450 px = 4-6 degrees).
